question.text: A 12% convertible bond of face value INR 1,000 has a conversion ratio of 25:1. If market price of the equity is INR 40 on the conversion date, what is the intrinsic equity value of the conversion option (excluding any bond value)?

explanation.text: The Logic: 25 shares * INR 40/share = INR 1,000, exactly equal to the bond face value. Conversion is AT-THE-MONEY; the option has only time value, no intrinsic premium to either party. The Trap: A is just the share price. C, D arbitrary. Cross-Exam Context: VIII (Derivatives) builds on convertible pricing. XIX-C covers same. Manager's Pro-Tip: An at-the-money convertible's delta is near 0.5; every INR 4 equity move above INR 40 adds INR 2 to bond intrinsic. Hedge by shorting ~12.5 shares per bond initially (0.5 delta * 25 conversion ratio) and re-hedge quarterly.
